key_insight: The Autonomy Index (AIx) offers a structured way to measure autonomous agency in clinical ethics, and human reviewers scored vignettes higher than language models overall.
clinical_relevance: This suggests general-purpose LLMs may underrepresent patient autonomy in ethics-related health responses, so their outputs should be checked carefully in autonomy-sensitive settings.
method: Built a 13-item Autonomy Index spanning Values Awareness, Factual Understanding, Rational Deliberation, and Intentional Action.
Compared trained human reviewers with multiple language models across 50 selected clinical ethics vignettes.
Used paired and mixed-effects analyses, plus agreement and variance checks, to compare human vs model scoring.
evidence_signal: Across the 50-vignette comparison set, human and model scores were strongly correlated (r=0.781), but humans scored higher by 11.0 points on average and case-level disagreement was wide.
watch_item: The vignette-based design and wide limits of agreement mean the index may not transfer cleanly to real-world patient encounters or to all clinical contexts.
paper_title: Auditing the Human LLM Autonomy Gap in Clinical Ethics: Development and Application of the Autonomy Index Across 50 Clinical Ethics Vignettes
